It's not just Samsung TVs — lots of other gadgets are spying on you

There's a little bit of sensationalism, I think. When using voice recognition many lower-powered devices won't have the onboard capacity to handle that voice recognition, so they offload that work to the cloud. These folks are disclosing that fact in their documentation, as they should. I don't see anything particularly wrong with that setup, nothing in any of these indicates that they're storing that data for marketing and analytics. Several of these explicitly state the data is destroyed at session end. Unless you want all devices to be handicapped by their onboard computing power, you'll have to deal with occasional use of cloud resources. Full disclosure and transparency is exactly what is needed in those cases, and is exactly what these manufacturers did albeit in some cases after being pressed to do so by the public.

Edit: The GPS stuff is a bit creepy, though, I admit.

Kind of glad I don't own most of these devices. My dad has Onstar in his truck, but other than that, we don't have any of these devices.

I personally run Debian Linux on everything, and I don't have a webcam on my desktop, only a mic. Even then, it usually isn't positioned well to capture sounds I make unless I move it when I want to use it.

A Pakistan northern provincial government will power 5,800 off-grid homes with a 200-watt solar panel for each family.

“The off-grid projects are a waste of time and money,” Senator Khan said. “These are temporary measures and are not sustainable.”

He contends that most recipients of the solar equipment will sell it for cash or let it deteriorate because they are too poor to maintain it.

“The government should start building small dams in the province as this would not only help generate enough electricity but also provide water for irrigation and drinking,” Senator Khan said.

The president of the Renewable and Alternative Energy Association of Pakistan, Naseer Ahmad said, nonetheless, that such solutions require recurring costs whereas only a one-time investment is necessary to fund solar energy.

These few lines allow one to understand the real issue. You hand someone with no money/food/etc something that is worth money, they turn around and sell it (plus making them pay 10% of the cost, which they don't have), give alternative idea (hydro power) but it costs more, takes longer to set up, has tons of other costs.

To summarize: We have a idea that we can do, but people might take the item and sell it or neglect it to death - this idea solves the issue short term, or we can build a dam/hydro which will solve the issue but will take years and will have annual costs on top. I like the first idea (give everyone solar panels).

My questions: do they get free electricity? When will they be added to on the grid? How long can you neglect the panel before it no longer works? Are they providing training seminars or are the expecting people to read the manual and run with it? There are more questions, but I would love to know more details.
